text:
All 16 tests now pass with `python3 -m unittest`. I didn't modify any tests.

Your three pre-reads:
- **(a) Directory read:** reading `catalog/` with the read tool returned "File not found", even though the directory exists. The error message suggested the same path back to me. I used `ls` instead.
- **(b) and (c) `books.py` reads:** lines 1–5 and lines 4–8 came back as expected. The offset is effectively 1-based in the output despite the tool's "0-based" description.

Fixes in `catalog/`:
- `books.py`: `parse_book` now converts `year` to `int`. This also fixed `test_age`.
- `search.py`: it imported `normalize` from a module that doesn't exist, so it now imports from `catalog.text`.
- `fees.py`: the fee was `days_late + DAILY_FEE`. It is now `days_late * DAILY_FEE`.
- `members.py`: `MAX_BORROWED` was 3 but the policy comment and the tests say five, so I set it to 5.
- `inventory.py`: `recent(n)` returned `n+1` events because of the `-n - 1` slice. It now returns the last `n`, and an empty list when `n` is 0 or less.
- `factory.py`: `sample_books()` was missing "Emma". I added `Book("Emma", "Austen", 1815, 1)`. The author, year and copies are my own choices, since the tests only check the title.
